events.title: Iran War Escalation
events.summary: The Iran war has escalated, leading to increased geopolitical instability in the Middle East. This has resulted in a surge in oil prices and a decline in stock markets. The US has imposed sanctions on Iran, which has further exacerbated the situation.
events.reasoning: The escalation of the Iran war has led to increased geopolitical instability, which is likely to result in higher oil prices and a decline in stock markets. Investing in oil services ETFs and shorting the S&P 500 ETF can provide a hedge against these market movements.

timeFrame.note: Monitor oil prices and stock market movements

events.exitStrategy: Exit when oil prices stabilize and stock markets recover

events.title: Nvidia AI Spending
events.summary: Nvidia has announced a multi-year technology partnership with SK hynix to advance memory for AI factories. This partnership is expected to increase Nvidia's AI spending and drive growth in the company's stock price.
events.reasoning: Nvidia's partnership with SK hynix is expected to drive growth in the company's AI spending and stock price. Investing in Nvidia can provide exposure to the growing AI market.

timeFrame.note: Monitor Nvidia's AI spending and stock price

events.exitStrategy: Exit when Nvidia's stock price reaches $500

gains.conservativeNote: If Nvidia's AI spending increases by 10%
gains.extendedNote: If Nvidia's AI spending increases by 20%

events.title: US Interest Rate Hike
events.summary: The US Federal Reserve is expected to hike interest rates in the coming months due to rising inflation and a strong job market. This is likely to result in a decline in stock markets and an increase in bond yields.
events.reasoning: The expected interest rate hike by the US Federal Reserve is likely to result in a decline in stock markets and an increase in bond yields. Shorting the S&P 500 ETF and investing in long-term Treasury bonds can provide a hedge against these market movements.

timeFrame.note: Monitor interest rates and stock market movements

events.exitStrategy: Exit when interest rates stabilize and stock markets recover
